hook: Shorten the day to about 1 h 24 min and the ground at the equator moves at orbital speed: you weigh nothing and float, one stride above an ordinary beach.

thumbnails.subject: a person seen from behind, floating a few centimetres above a flat equatorial beach, pebbles and dust lifting around their feet
thumbnails.composition: ground-level camera behind them; figure on the left third at ~40% frame height; low, gently curved horizon; empty sky right for text
thumbnails.lighting: the Sun as one long bright streak arcing across a blue-violet dawn sky (a very short day); warm rim light; magenta #EB63FF glow at the horizon
thumbnails.trigger: visual paradox and disbelief: an ordinary beach, and someone is floating
thumbnails.complements: the title asks what happens; the picture shows the strangest answer and a number the title doesn't explain

thumbnails.subject: the whole Earth, 3/4 view: the oceans gathered into a band around the equator, the high latitudes showing bare grey seabed
thumbnails.composition: globe centred-left, tilted so a pole faces the camera; black space right
thumbnails.lighting: hard sunlight from the right, night side soft; magenta rim on the atmosphere
thumbnails.trigger: scale shock: a planet without polar seas
thumbnails.complements: pairs with a floating or day-length title by adding a second, unexpected consequence

thumbnails.subject: a person at the equator, many faint shadows fanned around their feet like a sundial gone mad, the Sun a streak overhead
thumbnails.composition: high three-quarter view looking down, figure centred, shadows radiating
thumbnails.lighting: bright noon blur, clean ivory sand, magenta accents
thumbnails.complements: silent picture of a day lasting minutes; the title supplies the weight number

winner.title: What If Earth Spun Faster and Couldn't Stop?
winner.why: The title sets up the escalation and the picture jumps to the most impossible-looking moment: a person floating over an ordinary beach. The number on it is a second mystery the title doesn't answer.

notes: Truth: the film reaches weightlessness at about 1 h 24 min (c8), so the figure floats only slightly and doesn't fly upward. The poles running dry is in the oceans/poles beats (c6).
chatgptPrompt:
Create a YouTube thumbnail, 16:9 (1920x1080).
Subject: one person seen from behind, standing on a flat sandy beach at the equator, with their feet floating a few centimetres above the sand as if their weight has just switched off. Small pebbles and grains of sand are lifting off the ground around their feet.
Composition: low camera at ground level, slightly behind the person. The person is on the left third, about 40% of the frame height. The horizon is low and gently curved, with a wide empty sky on the right for the text.
Lighting and treatment: the Sun is a single long bright streak arcing across a deep blue-violet dawn sky, like a time-lapse of a very short day. Warm rim light on the person from the streak, a magenta (#EB63FF) glow near the horizon. Sharp foreground, soft background, high contrast, clean.
Mood: disbelief and wonder: are they floating?
Text: "84-MINUTE DAY" in heavy white condensed sans-serif, upper right, large, with a soft dark shadow. No other text.
Scientific accuracy: the person floats only slightly, weightless at ground level, not flying upward; the ground is ordinary Earth; the Sun streak shows a very fast day.
Avoid: no arrows, circles, faces with exaggerated expressions, logos, watermarks, brand names, extra text, spaceships, explosions, or anything that looks like a news photo.
Style: premium editorial science documentary, distinctive and art-directed, not generic AI art.

shortsCover.note: Part 1/Part 2 covers: use the floating moment for Part 2 and the 12-hour Sun race for Part 1.
